newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen down during KGHM offer.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen down during KGHM offer.

text.p: Polish shares extended Tuesday's slight fall and analysts said that though a gain was possible on Thursday, demand should stay low this week due to copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz's public offering ending Friday.
They said the bourse, after continuing its slight downtrend this week, could rebound from the falls once it got the KGHM offer behind it, as some stock prices were now attractive.

"In the short term it seems a rebound awaits us but at least tomorrow the money going to (KGHM Polska) Miedz will cause some supply (on the bourse)," said Robert Nejman, an analyst at Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index eased 0.1 percent to 15,066.6 points and turnover fell 9.2 percent to 192.4 million zlotys ($58.5 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 40 to 39 with 30 stocks flat.
Bank Handlowy, which rose 3.9 percent in heavy trade to 40 zlotys ($12.2), stole the show for the third session running since starting trade on Monday at 37.9 zlotys ($11.5), 8.3 percent above issue.
Analysts said the stock, whose 100.9-million-zloty ($30.7 million) turnover on Wednesday comprised 60 percent of main-market trade, could begin to stabilise.
Analysts said a good sign was the prime minister's Tuesday statement that 1998 GDP could rise five to six percent versus the government's previous forecast of 5-5.5 percent.

But they said there were still negative economic signals, including a central banker's recent statement that Poland faced a gaping current account deficit and a Czech-style financial crisis next year if it failed to balance the 1998 budget.
